steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Block printing uses carved stamps applied to fabric; screen printing forces ink through a mesh stencil — both can create repeat patterns.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Batik applies wax as a resist before dyeing — the wax blocks dye, creating patterns where the wax is removed.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Tie-dye and shibori create patterns through resist: binding, folding, twisting or compressing fabric before dyeing.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Repeat patterns use a single motif repeated systematically — half-drop, brick, mirror and random repeats create different visual effects.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Create a series of experimental studies exploring fabric printing and dyeing. Annotate your process. | Research an artist or designer who works with fabric printing and dyeing. Write a critical analysis of their approach and explain how it has informed your own work. | Evaluate the effectiveness of your experiments with fabric printing and dyeing. Which approaches were most successful and why?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A range of experimental studies showing different approaches to fabric printing and dyeing, each annotated with media, technique and purpose. Show development from initial experiments to refined outco | A critical analysis naming a specific artist/designer, using specialist vocabulary, explaining their context and approach, and making clear connections to personal work. | A reflective evaluation identifying successful and less successful experiments, explaining WHY using technical and conceptual language, and showing how evaluation led to further refinement.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Address ALL four Assessment Objectives — AO1 (develop), AO2 (refine), AO3 (record), AO4 (present) Show the FULL creative journey — from initial research to final outcome Annotate your work using specialist vocabulary (not just "I like it") Draw from primary sources wherever possible — real objects, not photos Experiment with a RANGE of media and techniques before selecting Make clear connections between artist research and your own developing work
